fields.sample_size: n = 3,047 households in 177 household clusters (primary sampling units), 2018 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey, spatially linked to provider data from an international utility database (IBNET) and NWASCO regulator reports; 11 water supply and sanitation companies
fields.covariates: Model 1: native language, month of interview (season), type of piped service, home ownership and provider dummies; Model 2 (provider-level model): the same significant household variables plus neighbourhood wealth, regulator-reported litres per capita per day, utility-level GDP per capita and their interactions; random effect for household cluster (ICC 0.27 and 0.31)
fields.section: Full text: Abstract; Methods; Results (Tables 1, 2 and 4); Discussion
fields.exact_location: Table 4 p.15 (multilevel logistic regression, n = 3,047, 177 clusters): at least partly owns the home OR 1.31 (SE 0.13) in Model 1 and 1.32 in Model 2, flagged *** (p < 0.01 per the table legend; the body text says p < 0.001); abstract and Results give 47% reporting an interruption (abstract 95% CI 45-49, results text 44-49), provider range 18-76% (results text 19-77%)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a multilevel analysis of 3,047 Zambian households linked to utility and regulator data finds that 47% reported at least one full day without piped water in the previous fortnight, with large differences between providers, and higher odds of interruption for home owners (OR 1.31); read in full text 2026-10-04.
pdf_note: PLOS Water 3(2):e0000127, 26 pages, English (Drive inbox file S104_Thomas_Possee_2024...pdf) read in full; figures and the supplementary tables (S1-S17) not read; the abstract and the body text give slightly different confidence limits and provider range for the same estimates
notes: The extraction already matched the abstract; the full text adds the cluster count, the covariate lists and the table location, and shows small internal inconsistencies in the paper.
